title: RMOS-CONVERGE-001B: production output census + retract capability convergence
intent: Phase 0/1 census of the live manufacturing-output surface taken from the mounted FastAPI route table (1062 routes, 62 machine-artifact emitters, 60 with no feasibility call, 5 self-minting a literal GREEN RunDecision), plus remediation of the one capability covered by an explicit owner ruling: retract. Every other discovered bypass is classified and reported at the checkpoint, not patched, per the owner ruling that the census may classify additional bypasses but may not take a newly discovered capability offline without explicit acceptance of that availability change.
behavior_change: INTENTIONAL - newly blocked production routes. All four mounted retract G-code routes (POST /api/cam/retract/gcode, /gcode_governed, /gcode/download, /gcode/download_governed) now return 409 SAFETY_BLOCKED instead of emitting G-code. Two of them previously built G-code and then minted a literal GREEN RunDecision around it; the other two bypassed RMOS entirely and served a .nc download with no run, decision or hash. There is no substantive retract feasibility evaluator, so the capability is blocked by design under the owner ruling of 2026-08-23. This is a fail-closed conversion of a live production capability, not an internal refactor. Also: tool_id moves from retract_gcode to retract:<strategy> and resolve_mode gains a retract: prefix so the capability blocks as a known operation rather than an unknown tool - this grants no evaluator (resolve_feasibility_engine for retract returns None) and changes no other route's behavior. No other capability was patched.

diff_articulation.what_changed: (1) retract_gcode_router.py restructured so authority precedes generation structurally rather than by statement order: _authorize_retract() calls the 001A canonical boundary, derives the decision via SafetyPolicy, persists a BLOCKED RunArtifact carrying the feasibility hash but no gcode_sha256 and no attachment, and raises 409; G-code construction moved into pure builders (_build_simple_retract_gcode, _build_download_retract_gcode) that contain no authority code and are reachable only after authorization returns; _persist_authorized_run binds an authorized artifact to the run that authorized it. The two _governed routes are retained as thin delegations to their plain counterparts, so the suffix no longer denotes a different lane. (2) rmos_feasibility_router.resolve_mode gains a retract: prefix - an identity/wiring fix permitted by the 001B handoff, not an evaluator-table expansion. (3) New census artifact records the base SHA, entry-gate verification, inclusion rule, full candidate triage with per-exclusion evidence, the Phase 1 deep matrix, retract pre/post witnesses, and the eleven ungoverned capabilities awaiting a ruling. (4) New test module with 19 witnesses covering B01, B07, B09, B13, B14 and B19, plus a structural guard that the builders contain no authority code and that no route constructs a literal GREEN RunDecision - checked on the AST rather than source text, so the module may still describe the retired anti-pattern in prose.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: Closes a live authority bypass on machine-consumable output. Before this change a caller blocked anywhere in RMOS could obtain retract G-code, as a .nc download, from a route that never consulted feasibility - and two sibling routes wrapped that same unassessed output in a governed-looking run with a self-minted GREEN decision. The census is not decoration: it establishes that retract is one instance of a pattern (five routes self-mint GREEN; only two of twenty-nine in-scope routes were governed before this tranche) and provides the blast-radius map the owner requires before authorizing the next cutover group.

retract identity probe -> retract:direct, retract:ramped, retract:helical all resolve mode=retract, engine=None, UNKNOWN, blocked, FEASIBILITY_ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE

files.intent: Converge all four retract G-code routes onto the 001A authority boundary; extract generation into pure builders reached only after authorization; persist BLOCKED attempts for audit without an executable artifact; retain the _governed paths as delegations carrying identical authority.
files.behavior_change: yes - all four routes now return 409 SAFETY_BLOCKED and emit no G-code

files.intent: Add a retract: prefix to resolve_mode so the capability blocks as a known operation with no authorized evaluator rather than as an unknown tool. Identity/wiring only; no engine registered.
files.behavior_change: none for any existing route - retract previously resolved to unknown and blocked; it now resolves to retract and blocks

files.intent: 19 witnesses: 001A boundary present, truthful retract identity, all four routes blocked by one authority, no machine output emitted (observable, no production seam added), client-declared authority cannot unblock, blocked attempts auditable, and a structural AST guard that generation cannot precede authorization and no route mints a literal GREEN decision.

The census artifact: base SHA and entry-gate provenance, inclusion rule, full candidate triage with per-exclusion evidence, Phase 1 deep matrix, retract pre/post witnesses, the eleven ungoverned capabilities awaiting a capability-level ruling, and preserved F7/F9/F10 deferrals.
Per-PR CBSP21 patch manifest enumerating every changed file.

Reconciliation: 28 tests assert that retract manufactures output (200, G-code body, .nc attachment, X-Run-ID, X-ToolBox-Lane), which the owner ruling makes impossible. Marked xfail(strict=True) with the reason and restore condition, assertions preserved verbatim as the contract to restore rather than rewritten to expect 409 - a rewritten assertion would keep passing once a retract evaluator lands and would then assert the wrong thing. 54 tests in the file are unaffected and still pass.
